raw_response:
I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I won’t do anything too fancy. On 4.1 mu, wheat and maize take turns on the same fields, and for a small household like mine, steady harvest matters more than chasing the highest yield. Last year, if wheat looked weak after winter, a little extra topdressing helped, so this year I’ll still put enough base fertilizer and leave some for jointing. Water costs money from the well, so I won’t irrigate blindly, but wheat in our place usually needs a few waterings to be safe. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, so there’s no time for slow work. I’ll keep the turnaround tight, do simple field prep, use a local hybrid seed that people around here trust, and give maize enough fertilizer to hold yield. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go yellow, but with only 4.1 mu I still watch every yuan. Most of the work my family can handle ourselves, and only if timing gets tight would I pay for a little machine or labor help.

For wheat, I will use enough base fertilizer and save one topdressing for jointing, because in our area wheat without water and fertilizer can lose yield quickly.
